edits.intended_fault: BX2 parent: a cited row that records NO parent_run_id is treated as a row of the anchored launch (missing parent defaults to own). A pre-binding row, or a native client that omits the field, then binds any receipt whose digest it carries. The binding suite's foreign-launch case sets parent_run_id explicitly, so only a row WITHOUT the field tells the original from the mutant.

BX1 launch: the anchored launch no longer has to be a TOP_LEVEL row; any single row carrying the manifest's launch_run_id (a RECEIPT row, a MUTATION_CHILD) stands as the launch. A bundle may then anchor to one of its own node executions, or to a mutation child, as 'the launch that produced it'.

BX2 kind: a cited row of launch_kind MUTATION_CHILD (a test run under a mutant, charged to the same ledger) may stand for the node execution that produced a receipt. The binding suite pins only TOP_LEVEL cited as a node run.

evidence.g_inv (the slice's reading of BX2): a cited row whose ONLY failing dimension is a missing receipt_sha256 is accepted as binding (backward compatibility with digest-less rows). ARTIFACT_SWAP and every receipt-edit-after-the-run become undetectable for such rows. binding.binding_reasons still reports BIND_DIGEST_MISSING; the client ignores it. The first 'if why:' in evidence.py is g_inv's (line 484 of the frozen file).

evidence.launch_unbound (BX1): when the bundle's run.json names a launch, THAT launch is used for the BX1 check and for the launch G-INV binds rows to, instead of the keeper-anchored manifest's. The bundle then chooses its own launch; a consistent substitute launch (its own TOP_LEVEL row, every node row re-parented to it) qualifies against a manifest that names another.
